svg.title: Amazon SQS
svg.desc: Amazon SQS. A managed message queue: consumers poll, a visibility timeout hides messages in flight, and repeated failures go to a dead-letter queue. Step 1, Where it sits: The API answers 202 once SQS has stored each order; a burst of 8 waits for three workers. Step 2, Receive, hide, delete: worker-1 gets m-17, hidden from the others for 60 s, then deletes it with its receipt handle. Step 3, Redelivery and the DLQ: worker-2 crashes; m-18 is back 60 s later. m-20 fails 5 times: orders-dlq, alarm, fix, redrive. Step 4, Standard, FIFO, limits: Standard: nearly unlimited throughput, best-effort order. FIFO: in order per group, no duplicates.

g.text: The API answers 202 once SQS has stored each order; a burst of 8 waits for three workers.
worker-1 gets m-17, hidden from the others for 60 s, then deletes it with its receipt handle.
worker-2 crashes; m-18 is back 60 s later. m-20 fails 5 times: orders-dlq, alarm, fix, redrive.
Standard: nearly unlimited throughput, best-effort order. FIFO: in order per group, no duplicates.
standard queue · nearly unlimited throughput, best-effort order
· received but not deleted: hidden from the others for 60 s
amber bar: what is left of the 60 s (sped up)
queue empty: worker-3's long poll waits (up to 20 s)
60 s after the receive, m-18 is visible again
An alarm on the depth of orders-dlq pages the on-call engineer.
After the fix, a redrive (StartMessageMoveTask) moves m-20 back to orders
as a new message, with a new message ID. Give the DLQ a longer retention.
Per group: in order, and no more while any are in flight. Groups run in parallel.
pay-2 resent with the same MessageDeduplicationId within 5 min: dropped
The burst waits in the queue;
each worker asks for the next
Each receive returns a new one;
Long job? Extend the 60 s with
card before it died, and m-18
